implementation_notes: The textbook C++ realization: an abstract State with virtual handlers, one class per concrete state, and a Context that owns the current state as std::unique_ptr<State> and replaces it with std::move; states receive Context& and transition through a set_state method. Virtual dispatch is what replaces the if/switch ladder, and std::make_unique keeps ownership explicit. This form is still the right one when states need identity, virtual hooks or reference semantics, for example when something observes or registers on a state object.
pitfalls: Polymorphic states need a virtual destructor; deleting through the base without one is undefined behaviour.
A shared state instance (static object or shared_ptr) must be immutable - per-context data belongs to Context, not to the state.
Putting concrete state classes in the Context header tightens the compile-time coupling; forward-declare and keep states in their own translation units.

variants.name: Value-semantic state machine with std::variant and std::visit
variants.implementation_notes: C++17 turns the states into a closed sum type: std::variant<Idle, Loading, Ready> lives by value inside the machine and std::visit with an overload set dispatches an event to the active alternative, returning the successor state. This removes heap traffic and dynamic dispatch, keeps the machine copyable and trivially destructible, and makes exhaustiveness explicit because every alternative must be handled. Prefer it for numerous short-lived machines; keep the polymorphic form when states are extensible from outside the translation unit or need identity.
pitfalls: std::visit requires every alternative to be handled; a generic auto lambda silently swallows states added later, so prefer explicit overloads plus a static_assert on exhaustiveness.
Visiting by value copies the state; take alternatives by const reference unless the transition deliberately consumes them.
A variant becomes valueless_by_exception after a throwing assignment; check the flag if state constructors can throw.
